title: Google's November 2026 Core Update: What a Local Business Should Do
description: Google began a broad search update on 10 November that can shift rankings for about two weeks. What it is, and what is (and is not) worth doing.

answer.question: What is Google's November 2026 core update and should I worry?
answer.text: It is a general change to Google Search, not a penalty on any website: it started on 10 November 2026 and can take up to two weeks to finish rolling out.

intro: Google has started its November 2026 core update, a general search change that can move rankings for a couple of weeks. Here is what it is and how a local business should react.

body.text: On 10 November 2026 Google confirmed the start of a core update to its search engine. According to Google's own announcement, it applies worldwide and in all languages, and can take up to two weeks to complete.

Google describes it as a regular update meant to show more relevant, useful content to searchers, from all kinds of websites. It does not single out a particular page or business: it changes how many pages are assessed at once. That is why, during these days, it is normal to see rankings go up and down without you having done anything.

What to do: do not panic, and do not rebuild your website in a rush while the rollout lasts. When it finishes, wait a week and compare your visits and queries in Search Console with the week before 10 November. Only if you see a large, sustained drop does it make sense to review which pages were affected and improve their content.

What always helps, with or without an update: pages that genuinely answer what your customer is asking, clear information about your business (address, opening hours, services) and a complete, up-to-date Google Business Profile listing. This practical advice is ours, not an instruction from Google.
If you want to understand how to measure these changes, see the guide to using Search Console and Analytics in the LevanteHUB Academy.
